summary: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a Little Blackwater tower under Blackwater NWR as gone; no source read gives its build date, staffing or site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association. None of the sources checked describes the site today.

evidence.supports: association lists the Little Blackwater tower in Dorchester County as gone
evidence.quote: Blackwater NWR – Little Blackwater Dorchester 38.43727 -76.09234 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: association says it is unclear whether towers on wildlife refuges were for fire detection or wildlife observation
evidence.quote: there are questions whether several towers on wildlife refuges were for fire detection or wildlife observation

evidence.supports: association keeps these towers listed because definitive proof is lacking
evidence.quote: with lack of definitive proof, have been included

evidence.supports: association counts the Fish and Wildlife Service as one of the recognized federal wildland fire agencies
evidence.quote: since US Fish & Wildlife Service is one of the recognized federal wildland fire agencies

evidence.supports: refuge established in 1933 as a sanctuary for birds migrating along the Atlantic Flyway
evidence.quote: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1933 as a waterfowl sanctuary for birds migrating along the Atlantic Flyway.

evidence.supports: Wildlife Drive open to visitors with a daily or annual pass, by vehicle, bicycle or foot
evidence.quote: A daily or annual pass provides access to the refuge's 4-mile Wildlife Drive, which can be travelled by vehicle, bicycle, or foot

evidence.supports: most of the Wildlife Drive is closed on some listed deer-hunt dates
evidence.quote: the majority of Wildlife Drive will be CLOSED on the following dates for deer management hunts

notes_for_editor: The association list is the only source that mentions this tower, and it gives only the status (gone). No build date, builder, height, staffing, fire or site description turned up in the pages read. The association's general note says it is unclear whether refuge towers were for fire detection or wildlife observation; no source says which this one was. The Blackwater NWR pages read (FWS, Friends of Blackwater history, Wikipedia) do not mention a lookout tower. Searches used: 3 (one over the cap of 2, because a shared Blackwater query covered both Blackwater towers). Pages read: about 6 distinct pages. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story now says the sources checked, not all published sources, do not describe the site; the drive-access sentence now quotes the FWS page in full and notes the deer-hunt closures listed on the same page.
